verses.restored: Then therefore Pilate took Jesus and flogged him.

familiar.text: Then Pilate therefore took Jesus, and scourged him.

modern.text: Then Pilate took Jesus and had Him flogged.

original.text: Τότε οὖν ἔλαβεν ὁ Πιλᾶτος τὸν Ἰησοῦν καὶ ἐμαστίγωσεν.

verses.restored: The soldiers, weaving a crown from thorns, placed it on his head and threw a purple garment around him.

familiar.text: And the soldiers platted a crown of thorns, and put it on his head, and they put on him a purple robe,

modern.text: The soldiers twisted together a crown of thorns, set it on His head, and dressed Him in a purple robe.

original.text: καὶ οἱ στρατιῶται πλέξαντες στέφανον ἐξ ἀκανθῶν ἐπέθηκαν αὐτοῦ τῇ κεφαλῇ, καὶ ἱμάτιον πορφυροῦν περιέβαλον αὐτόν,

verses.restored: They were coming to him and saying, Hail, king of the Judeans, and giving him strikes.

familiar.text: And said, Hail, King of the Jews! and they smote him with their hands.

modern.text: And they went up to Him again and again, saying, “Hail, King of the Jews!” and slapping Him in the face.

original.text: καὶ ⸂ἤρχοντο πρὸς αὐτὸν καὶ⸃ ἔλεγον· Χαῖρε, ὁ βασιλεὺς τῶν Ἰουδαίων· καὶ ἐδίδοσαν αὐτῷ ῥαπίσματα.

verses.restored: Pilate went outside again and says to them, Look, I bring him out to you so that you may know I find no cause in him.

familiar.text: Pilate therefore went forth again, and saith unto them, Behold, I bring him forth to you, that ye may know that I find no fault in him.

modern.text: Once again Pilate came out and said to the Jews, “Look, I am bringing Him out to you to let you know that I find no basis for a charge against Him.”

original.text: ⸂καὶ ἐξῆλθεν⸃ πάλιν ἔξω ὁ Πιλᾶτος καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Ἴδε ἄγω ὑμῖν αὐτὸν ἔξω, ἵνα γνῶτε ὅτι ⸂οὐδεμίαν αἰτίαν εὑρίσκω ἐν αὐτῷ⸃.

verses.restored: Jesus therefore came out, wearing the thorn crown and purple garment. Pilate says to them, Look, the human.

familiar.text: Then came Jesus forth, wearing the crown of thorns, and the purple robe. And Pilate saith unto them, Behold the man!

modern.text: When Jesus came out wearing the crown of thorns and the purple robe, Pilate said to them, “Here is the man!”

original.text: ἐξῆλθεν οὖν ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἔξω, φορῶν τὸν ἀκάνθινον στέφανον καὶ τὸ πορφυροῦν ἱμάτιον. καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· ⸀Ἰδοὺ ὁ ἄνθρωπος.

verses.restored: When therefore the chief priests and officers saw him, they cried out, saying, Crucify, crucify. Pilate says to them, You take him and crucify, for I find no cause in him.

familiar.text: When the chief priests therefore and officers saw him, they cried out, saying, Crucify him, crucify him. Pilate saith unto them, Take ye him, and crucify him: for I find no fault in him.

modern.text: As soon as the chief priests and officers saw Him, they shouted, “Crucify Him! Crucify Him!” “You take Him and crucify Him,” Pilate replied, “for I find no basis for a charge against Him.”

original.text: ὅτε οὖν εἶδον αὐτὸν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ ὑπηρέται ἐκραύγασαν λέγοντες· Σταύρωσον ⸀σταύρωσον. λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Πιλᾶτος· Λάβετε αὐτὸν ὑμεῖς καὶ σταυρώσατε, ἐγὼ γὰρ οὐχ εὑρίσκω ἐν αὐτῷ αἰτίαν.

verses.restored: The Judeans answered him, We have a Law, and according to the Law he ought to die, because he made himself Son of the Divine.

familiar.text: The Jews answered him, We have a law, and by our law he ought to die, because he made himself the Son of God.

modern.text: “We have a law,” answered the Jews, “and according to that law He must die, because He declared Himself to be the Son of God.”

original.text: ἀπεκρίθησαν αὐτῷ οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι· Ἡμεῖς νόμον ἔχομεν, καὶ κατὰ τὸν ⸀νόμον ὀφείλει ἀποθανεῖν, ὅτι ⸂υἱὸν θεοῦ ἑαυτὸν⸃ ἐποίησεν.

verses.restored: When Pilate therefore heard this word, he was more afraid.

familiar.text: When Pilate therefore heard that saying, he was the more afraid;

modern.text: When Pilate heard this statement, he was even more afraid,

original.text: Ὅτε οὖν ἤκουσεν ὁ Πιλᾶτος τοῦτον τὸν λόγον, μᾶλλον ἐφοβήθη,

verses.restored: He entered the praetorium again and says to Jesus, From where are you? But Jesus gave him no answer.

familiar.text: And went again into the judgment hall, and saith unto Jesus, Whence art thou? But Jesus gave him no answer.

modern.text: and he went back into the Praetorium. “Where are You from?” he asked. But Jesus gave no answer.

original.text: καὶ εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὸ πραιτώριον πάλιν καὶ λέγει τῷ Ἰησοῦ· Πόθεν εἶ σύ; ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἀπόκρισιν οὐκ ἔδωκεν αὐτῷ.

verses.restored: Pilate therefore says to him, You do not speak to me? Do you not know that I have authority to release you and authority to crucify you?

familiar.text: Then saith Pilate unto him, Speakest thou not unto me? knowest thou not that I have power to crucify thee, and have power to release thee?

modern.text: So Pilate said to Him, “Do You refuse to speak to me? Do You not know that I have authority to release You and authority to crucify You?”

original.text: λέγει οὖν αὐτῷ ὁ Πιλᾶτος· Ἐμοὶ οὐ λαλεῖς; οὐκ οἶδας ὅτι ἐξουσίαν ἔχω ⸂ἀπολῦσαί σε καὶ ἐξουσίαν ἔχω σταυρῶσαί⸃ σε;

verses.restored: Jesus answered him, You would have no authority against me unless it had been given to you from above; because of this the one handing me over to you has greater sin/misalignment.

familiar.text: Jesus answered, Thou couldest have no power at all against me, except it were given thee from above: therefore he that delivered me unto thee hath the greater sin.

modern.text: Jesus answered, “You would have no authority over Me if it were not given to you from above. Therefore the one who handed Me over to you is guilty of greater sin.”

original.text: ἀπεκρίθη ⸀αὐτῷ Ἰησοῦς· Οὐκ εἶχες ἐξουσίαν ⸂κατʼ ἐμοῦ οὐδεμίαν⸃ εἰ μὴ ἦν ⸂δεδομένον σοι⸃ ἄνωθεν· διὰ τοῦτο ὁ ⸀παραδούς μέ σοι μείζονα ἁμαρτίαν ἔχει.

verses.restored: From this Pilate was seeking to release him, but the Judeans cried out, saying, If you release this one, you are not Caesar's friend; everyone making himself king opposes Caesar.

familiar.text: And from thenceforth Pilate sought to release him: but the Jews cried out, saying, If thou let this man go, thou art not Caesar’s friend: whosoever maketh himself a king speaketh against Caesar.

modern.text: From then on, Pilate tried to release Him, but the Jews kept shouting, “If you release this man, you are no friend of Caesar. Anyone who declares himself a king is defying Caesar.”

original.text: ἐκ τούτου ⸂ὁ Πιλᾶτος ἐζήτει⸃ ἀπολῦσαι αὐτόν· οἱ δὲ Ἰουδαῖοι ⸀ἐκραύγασαν λέγοντες· Ἐὰν τοῦτον ἀπολύσῃς, οὐκ εἶ φίλος τοῦ Καίσαρος· πᾶς ὁ βασιλέα ἑαυτὸν ποιῶν ἀντιλέγει τῷ Καίσαρι.

verses.restored: Pilate therefore, hearing these words, brought Jesus outside and sat on the judgment seat at a place called Stone Pavement, and in Hebrew Gabbatha.

familiar.text: When Pilate therefore heard that saying, he brought Jesus forth, and sat down in the judgment seat in a place that is called the Pavement, but in the Hebrew, Gabbatha.

modern.text: When Pilate heard these words, he brought Jesus out and sat on the judgment seat at a place called the Stone Pavement, which in Hebrew is Gabbatha.

original.text: Ὁ οὖν Πιλᾶτος ἀκούσας ⸂τῶν λόγων τούτων⸃ ἤγαγεν ἔξω τὸν Ἰησοῦν, καὶ ἐκάθισεν ⸀ἐπὶ βήματος εἰς τόπον λεγόμενον Λιθόστρωτον, Ἑβραϊστὶ δὲ Γαββαθα.

verses.restored: It was Preparation of the Passover, about the sixth hour. He says to the Judeans, Look, your king.

familiar.text: And it was the preparation of the passover, and about the sixth hour: and he saith unto the Jews, Behold your King!

modern.text: It was the day of Preparation for the Passover, about the sixth hour. And Pilate said to the Jews, “Here is your King!”

original.text: ἦν δὲ παρασκευὴ τοῦ πάσχα, ὥρα ⸂ἦν ὡς⸃ ἕκτη. καὶ λέγει τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις· Ἴδε ὁ βασιλεὺς ὑμῶν.

verses.restored: They therefore cried out, Take away, take away, crucify him. Pilate says to them, Shall I crucify your king? The chief priests answered, We have no king except Caesar.

familiar.text: But they cried out, Away with him, away with him, crucify him. Pilate saith unto them, Shall I crucify your King? The chief priests answered, We have no king but Caesar.

modern.text: At this, they shouted, “Away with Him! Away with Him! Crucify Him!” “Shall I crucify your King?” Pilate asked. “We have no king but Caesar,” replied the chief priests. The Crucifixion (Psalms 22:1–31; Matthew 27:32–44; Mark 15:21–32; Luke 23:26–43)

original.text: ⸂ἐκραύγασαν οὖν ἐκεῖνοι⸃· Ἆρον ἆρον, σταύρωσον αὐτόν. λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Πιλᾶτος· Τὸν βασιλέα ὑμῶν σταυρώσω; ἀπεκρίθησαν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς· Οὐκ ἔχομεν βασιλέα εἰ μὴ Καίσαρα.

verses.restored: Then therefore he handed him over to them so that he might be crucified. They took Jesus.

familiar.text: Then delivered he him therefore unto them to be crucified. And they took Jesus, and led him away.

modern.text: Then Pilate handed Jesus over to be crucified, and the soldiers took Him away.

original.text: τότε οὖν παρέδωκεν αὐτὸν αὐτοῖς ἵνα σταυρωθῇ. Παρέλαβον ⸀οὖν τὸν ⸀Ἰησοῦν·

verses.restored: Carrying the cross for himself, he went out to the place called Skull Place, which is called in Hebrew Golgotha.

familiar.text: And he bearing his cross went forth into a place called the place of a skull, which is called in the Hebrew Golgotha:

modern.text: Carrying His own cross, He went out to The Place of the Skull, which in Hebrew is called Golgotha.

original.text: καὶ βαστάζων ⸂αὑτῷ τὸν σταυρὸν⸃ ἐξῆλθεν εἰς ⸀τὸν λεγόμενον Κρανίου Τόπον, ⸀ὃ λέγεται Ἑβραϊστὶ Γολγοθα,

verses.restored: There they crucified him, and with him two others, on this side and that side, and Jesus in the middle.

familiar.text: Where they crucified him, and two other with him, on either side one, and Jesus in the midst.

modern.text: There they crucified Him, and with Him two others, one on each side, with Jesus in the middle.

original.text: ὅπου αὐτὸν ἐσταύρωσαν, καὶ μετʼ αὐτοῦ ἄλλους δύο ἐντεῦθεν καὶ ἐντεῦθεν, μέσον δὲ τὸν Ἰησοῦν.

verses.restored: Pilate also wrote a title and placed it on the cross. It was written: Jesus the Nazarene, the King of the Judeans.

familiar.text: And Pilate wrote a title, and put it on the cross. And the writing was, JESUS OF NAZARETH THE KING OF THE JEWS.

modern.text: Pilate also had a notice posted on the cross. It read: JESUS OF NAZARETH, THE KING OF THE JEWS.

original.text: ἔγραψεν δὲ καὶ τίτλον ὁ Πιλᾶτος καὶ ἔθηκεν ἐπὶ τοῦ σταυροῦ· ἦν δὲ γεγραμμένον· Ἰησοῦς ὁ Ναζωραῖος ὁ βασιλεὺς τῶν Ἰουδαίων.

verses.restored: Many of the Judeans read this title, because the place where Jesus was crucified was near the city; and it was written in Hebrew, Latin, and Greek.

familiar.text: This title then read many of the Jews: for the place where Jesus was crucified was nigh to the city: and it was written in Hebrew, and Greek, and Latin.

modern.text: Many of the Jews read this sign, because the place where Jesus was crucified was near the city, and it was written in Hebrew, Latin, and Greek.

original.text: τοῦτον οὖν τὸν τίτλον πολλοὶ ἀνέγνωσαν τῶν Ἰουδαίων, ὅτι ἐγγὺς ἦν ὁ τόπος τῆς πόλεως ὅπου ἐσταυρώθη ὁ Ἰησοῦς· καὶ ἦν γεγραμμένον Ἑβραϊστί, ⸂Ῥωμαϊστί, Ἑλληνιστί⸃.

verses.restored: Therefore the chief priests of the Judeans said to Pilate, Do not write, The King of the Judeans, but that he said, I am King of the Judeans.

familiar.text: Then said the chief priests of the Jews to Pilate, Write not, The King of the Jews; but that he said, I am King of the Jews.

modern.text: So the chief priests of the Jews said to Pilate, “Do not write, ‘The King of the Jews,’ but only that He said, ‘I am the King of the Jews.’”

original.text: ἔλεγον οὖν τῷ Πιλάτῳ οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς τῶν Ἰουδαίων· Μὴ γράφε· Ὁ βασιλεὺς τῶν Ἰουδαίων, ἀλλʼ ὅτι ἐκεῖνος εἶπεν Βασιλεὺς ⸂τῶν Ἰουδαίων εἰμί⸃.

verses.restored: Pilate answered, What I have written, I have written.

familiar.text: Pilate answered, What I have written I have written.

modern.text: Pilate answered, “What I have written, I have written.”

original.text: ἀπεκρίθη ὁ Πιλᾶτος· Ὃ γέγραφα γέγραφα.

verses.restored: The soldiers therefore, when they crucified Jesus, took his garments and made four parts, a part for each soldier, and the tunic. The tunic was seamless, woven from above through the whole.

familiar.text: Then the soldiers, when they had crucified Jesus, took his garments, and made four parts, to every soldier a part; and also his coat: now the coat was without seam, woven from the top throughout.

modern.text: When the soldiers had crucified Jesus, they divided His garments into four parts, one for each soldier, with the tunic remaining. It was seamless, woven in one piece from top to bottom.

original.text: οἱ οὖν στρατιῶται ὅτε ἐσταύρωσαν τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἔλαβον τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐποίησαν τέσσαρα μέρη, ἑκάστῳ στρατιώτῃ μέρος, καὶ τὸν χιτῶνα. ἦν δὲ ὁ χιτὼν ἄραφος, ἐκ τῶν ἄνωθεν ὑφαντὸς διʼ ὅλου·

verses.restored: They said to one another, Let us not tear it, but cast lots for it, whose it will be, so that the Scripture might be fulfilled: They divided my garments among themselves, and for my clothing they cast lots. Therefore the soldiers did these things.

familiar.text: They said therefore among themselves, Let us not rend it, but cast lots for it, whose it shall be: that the scripture might be fulfilled, which saith, They parted my raiment among them, and for my vesture they did cast lots. These things therefore the soldiers did.

modern.text: So they said to one another, “Let us not tear it. Instead, let us cast lots to see who will get it.” This was to fulfill the Scripture: “They divided My garments among them, and cast lots for My clothing.” So that is what the soldiers did.

original.text: εἶπαν οὖν πρὸς ἀλλήλους· Μὴ σχίσωμεν αὐτόν, ἀλλὰ λάχωμεν περὶ αὐτοῦ τίνος ἔσται· ἵνα ἡ γραφὴ πληρωθῇ ⸂ἡ λέγουσα⸃· Διεμερίσαντο τὰ ἱμάτιά μου ἑαυτοῖς καὶ ἐπὶ τὸν ἱματισμόν μου ἔβαλον κλῆρον. Οἱ μὲν οὖν στρατιῶται ταῦτα ἐποίησαν.

verses.restored: Standing by the cross of Jesus were his mother, his mother's sister, Mary of Clopas, and Mary Magdalene.

familiar.text: Now there stood by the cross of Jesus his mother, and his mother’s sister, Mary the wife of Cleophas, and Mary Magdalene.

modern.text: Near the cross of Jesus stood His mother and her sister, as well as Mary the wife of Clopas and Mary Magdalene.

original.text: Εἱστήκεισαν δὲ παρὰ τῷ σταυρῷ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ἡ μήτηρ αὐτοῦ καὶ ἡ ἀδελφὴ τῆς μητρὸς αὐτοῦ, Μαρία ἡ τοῦ Κλωπᾶ καὶ Μαρία ἡ Μαγδαληνή.

verses.restored: Jesus therefore, seeing the mother and the disciple whom he loved standing by, says to the mother, Woman, look, your son.

familiar.text: When Jesus therefore saw his mother, and the disciple standing by, whom he loved, he saith unto his mother, Woman, behold thy son!

modern.text: When Jesus saw His mother and the disciple whom He loved standing nearby, He said to His mother, “Woman, here is your son.”

original.text: Ἰησοῦς οὖν ἰδὼν τὴν μητέρα καὶ τὸν μαθητὴν παρεστῶτα ὃν ἠγάπα λέγει τῇ ⸀μητρί· Γύναι, ⸀ἴδε ὁ υἱός σου·

verses.restored: Then he says to the disciple, Look, your mother. And from that hour the disciple took her into his own.

familiar.text: Then saith he to the disciple, Behold thy mother! And from that hour that disciple took her unto his own home.

modern.text: Then He said to the disciple, “Here is your mother.” So from that hour, this disciple took her into his home. The Death of Jesus (Psalms 22:1–31; Matthew 27:45–56; Mark 15:33–41; Luke 23:44–49)

original.text: εἶτα λέγει τῷ μαθητῇ· ⸀Ἴδε ἡ μήτηρ σου. καὶ ἀπʼ ἐκείνης τῆς ὥρας ἔλαβεν ὁ μαθητὴς αὐτὴν εἰς τὰ ἴδια.

verses.restored: After this, Jesus, knowing that all things had already been completed, so that the Scripture might be completed, says, I thirst.

familiar.text: After this, Jesus knowing that all things were now accomplished, that the scripture might be fulfilled, saith, I thirst.

modern.text: After this, knowing that everything had now been accomplished, and to fulfill the Scripture, Jesus said, “I am thirsty.”

original.text: Μετὰ τοῦτο ⸀εἰδὼς ὁ Ἰησοῦς ὅτι ⸂ἤδη πάντα⸃ τετέλεσται ἵνα τελειωθῇ ἡ γραφὴ λέγει· Διψῶ.

verses.restored: A vessel full of sour wine was set there; therefore putting a sponge full of sour wine around hyssop, they brought it to his mouth.

familiar.text: Now there was set a vessel full of vinegar: and they filled a spunge with vinegar, and put it upon hyssop, and put it to his mouth.

modern.text: A jar of sour wine was sitting there. So they soaked a sponge in the wine, put it on a stalk of hyssop, and lifted it to His mouth.

original.text: ⸀σκεῦος ἔκειτο ὄξους μεστόν· ⸂σπόγγον οὖν μεστὸν τοῦ⸃ ὄξους ⸀ὑσσώπῳ περιθέντες προσήνεγκαν αὐτοῦ τῷ στόματι.

verses.restored: When therefore Jesus received the sour wine, he said, It has been completed. And bowing the head, he handed over the spirit.

familiar.text: When Jesus therefore had received the vinegar, he said, It is finished: and he bowed his head, and gave up the ghost.

modern.text: When Jesus had received the sour wine, He said, “It is finished.” And bowing His head, He yielded up His spirit. Jesus’ Side Is Pierced (Zechariah 12:10–14)

original.text: ὅτε οὖν ἔλαβεν τὸ ὄξος ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Τετέλεσται, καὶ κλίνας τὴν κεφαλὴν παρέδωκεν τὸ πνεῦμα.

verses.restored: Therefore the Judeans, since it was Preparation, so that the bodies might not remain on the cross on the Sabbath, for that Sabbath was a great day, asked Pilate that their legs might be broken and they taken away.

familiar.text: The Jews therefore, because it was the preparation, that the bodies should not remain upon the cross on the sabbath day, (for that sabbath day was an high day,) besought Pilate that their legs might be broken, and that they might be taken away.

modern.text: It was the day of Preparation, and the next day was a High Sabbath. In order that the bodies would not remain on the cross during the Sabbath, the Jews asked Pilate to have the legs broken and the bodies removed.

original.text: Οἱ οὖν Ἰουδαῖοι, ⸂ἐπεὶ παρασκευὴ ἦν, ἵνα μὴ μείνῃ ἐπὶ τοῦ σταυροῦ τὰ σώματα ἐν τῷ σαββάτῳ⸃, ἦν γὰρ μεγάλη ἡ ἡμέρα ἐκείνου τοῦ σαββάτου, ἠρώτησαν τὸν Πιλᾶτον ἵνα κατεαγῶσιν αὐτῶν τὰ σκέλη καὶ ἀρθῶσιν.

verses.restored: Therefore the soldiers came and broke the legs of the first and of the other crucified with him.

familiar.text: Then came the soldiers, and brake the legs of the first, and of the other which was crucified with him.

modern.text: So the soldiers came and broke the legs of the first man who had been crucified with Jesus, and those of the other.

original.text: ἦλθον οὖν οἱ στρατιῶται, καὶ τοῦ μὲν πρώτου κατέαξαν τὰ σκέλη καὶ τοῦ ἄλλου τοῦ συσταυρωθέντος αὐτῷ·

verses.restored: But coming to Jesus, when they saw he had already died, they did not break his legs.

familiar.text: But when they came to Jesus, and saw that he was dead already, they brake not his legs:

modern.text: But when they came to Jesus and saw that He was already dead, they did not break His legs.

original.text: ἐπὶ δὲ τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἐλθόντες, ὡς εἶδον ⸂ἤδη αὐτὸν⸃ τεθνηκότα, οὐ κατέαξαν αὐτοῦ τὰ σκέλη,

verses.restored: But one of the soldiers pierced his side with a spear, and immediately blood and water came out.

familiar.text: But one of the soldiers with a spear pierced his side, and forthwith came there out blood and water.

modern.text: Instead, one of the soldiers pierced His side with a spear, and immediately blood and water flowed out.

original.text: ἀλλʼ εἷς τῶν στρατιωτῶν λόγχῃ αὐτοῦ τὴν πλευρὰν ἔνυξεν, καὶ ⸂ἐξῆλθεν εὐθὺς⸃ αἷμα καὶ ὕδωρ.

verses.restored: The one having seen has borne witness, and his witness is true; and that one knows that he says true things, so that you also may trust.

familiar.text: And he that saw it bare record, and his record is true: and he knoweth that he saith true, that ye might believe.

modern.text: The one who saw it has testified to this, and his testimony is true. He knows that he is telling the truth, so that you also may believe.

original.text: καὶ ὁ ἑωρακὼς μεμαρτύρηκεν, καὶ ἀληθινὴ ⸂αὐτοῦ ἐστιν⸃ ἡ μαρτυρία, καὶ ἐκεῖνος οἶδεν ὅτι ἀληθῆ λέγει, ἵνα ⸀καὶ ὑμεῖς ⸀πιστεύητε.

verses.restored: For these things happened so that the Scripture might be fulfilled: Not a bone of him will be broken.

familiar.text: For these things were done, that the scripture should be fulfilled, A bone of him shall not be broken.

modern.text: Now these things happened so that the Scripture would be fulfilled: “Not one of His bones will be broken.”

original.text: ἐγένετο γὰρ ταῦτα ἵνα ἡ γραφὴ πληρωθῇ· Ὀστοῦν οὐ συντριβήσεται ⸀αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: And again another Scripture says: They will look on the one whom they pierced.

familiar.text: And again another scripture saith, They shall look on him whom they pierced.

modern.text: And, as another Scripture says: “They will look on the One they have pierced.” The Burial of Jesus (Isaiah 53:9–12; Matthew 27:57–61; Mark 15:42–47; Luke 23:50–56)

original.text: καὶ πάλιν ἑτέρα γραφὴ λέγει· Ὄψονται εἰς ὃν ἐξεκέντησαν.

verses.restored: After these things Joseph from Arimathea, being a disciple of Jesus but hidden because of fear of the Judeans, asked Pilate that he might take the body of Jesus; and Pilate permitted it. He came therefore and took his body.

familiar.text: And after this Joseph of Arimathaea, being a disciple of Jesus, but secretly for fear of the Jews, besought Pilate that he might take away the body of Jesus: and Pilate gave him leave. He came therefore, and took the body of Jesus.

modern.text: Afterward, Joseph of Arimathea, who was a disciple of Jesus (but secretly for fear of the Jews), asked Pilate to let him remove the body of Jesus. Pilate gave him permission, so he came and removed His body.

original.text: Μετὰ ⸀δὲ ταῦτα ἠρώτησεν τὸν Πιλᾶτον Ἰωσὴφ ⸀ἀπὸ Ἁριμαθαίας, ὢν μαθητὴς τοῦ Ἰησοῦ κεκρυμμένος δὲ διὰ τὸν φόβον τῶν Ἰουδαίων, ἵνα ἄρῃ τὸ σῶμα τοῦ Ἰησοῦ· καὶ ἐπέτρεψεν ὁ Πιλᾶτος. ἦλθεν οὖν καὶ ἦρεν τὸ σῶμα ⸀αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: Nicodemus also came, the one who first came to him by night, bringing a mixture of myrrh and aloes, about a hundred litrai.

familiar.text: And there came also Nicodemus, which at the first came to Jesus by night, and brought a mixture of myrrh and aloes, about an hundred pound weight.

modern.text: Nicodemus, who had previously come to Jesus at night, also brought a mixture of myrrh and aloes, about seventy-five pounds.

original.text: ἦλθεν δὲ καὶ Νικόδημος, ὁ ἐλθὼν πρὸς ⸀αὐτὸν νυκτὸς τὸ πρῶτον, φέρων ⸀μίγμα σμύρνης καὶ ἀλόης ὡς λίτρας ἑκατόν.

verses.restored: They took the body of Jesus and bound it in linen cloths with the spices, as is burial custom among the Judeans.

familiar.text: Then took they the body of Jesus, and wound it in linen clothes with the spices, as the manner of the Jews is to bury.

modern.text: So they took the body of Jesus and wrapped it in linen cloths with the spices, according to the Jewish burial custom.

original.text: ἔλαβον οὖν τὸ σῶμα τοῦ Ἰησοῦ καὶ ἔδησαν ⸀αὐτὸ ὀθονίοις μετὰ τῶν ἀρωμάτων, καθὼς ἔθος ἐστὶν τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις ἐνταφιάζειν.

verses.restored: In the place where he was crucified there was a garden, and in the garden a new tomb in which no one had ever yet been laid.

familiar.text: Now in the place where he was crucified there was a garden; and in the garden a new sepulchre, wherein was never man yet laid.

modern.text: Now there was a garden in the place where Jesus was crucified, and in the garden a new tomb in which no one had yet been laid.

original.text: ἦν δὲ ἐν τῷ τόπῳ ὅπου ἐσταυρώθη κῆπος, καὶ ἐν τῷ κήπῳ μνημεῖον καινόν, ἐν ᾧ οὐδέπω οὐδεὶς ⸂ἦν τεθειμένος⸃·

verses.restored: There therefore, because of the Judean Preparation, because the tomb was near, they laid Jesus.

familiar.text: There laid they Jesus therefore because of the Jews’ preparation day; for the sepulchre was nigh at hand.

modern.text: And because it was the Jewish day of Preparation and the tomb was nearby, they placed Jesus there.

original.text: ἐκεῖ οὖν διὰ τὴν παρασκευὴν τῶν Ἰουδαίων, ὅτι ἐγγὺς ἦν τὸ μνημεῖον, ἔθηκαν τὸν Ἰησοῦν.
